title: A drunken world
summary: In the last days, the nations of the Gentiles and the Jews are described as drunken with iniquity and abominations. The Lord of Hosts will visit them with thunder, earthquake, noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire.

explicit_facts.text: In the last days, the nations of the Gentiles and the Jews, on this land and other lands, will be drunken with iniquity and abominations.
The Lord of Hosts will visit them with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A symbolic view of people and lands amid storm imagery may convey the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities, clothing, and exact setting are not specified.
The form or visible appearance of the Lord of Hosts is not specified.

narration.text: in the last days
they will be drunken with iniquity
they shall be visited of the Lord of Hosts

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The visitation is prophesied; do not depict it as a separately narrated event already occurring.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a specific historical disaster or portray a divine figure not visually described.

title: An empty dream
summary: The nations fighting against Mount Zion are compared to a hungry or thirsty person who dreams of eating or drinking, then wakes still unsatisfied.

explicit_facts.text: Nations fighting against Zion are compared to a hungry or thirsty person whose dream does not satisfy them upon waking.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The comparison may be conveyed with separate symbolic dream imagery, not as a literal event.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of any dreamer are not specified.

narration.text: as a dream of a night vision
he awaketh and his soul is empty

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The hunger and thirst are figures of speech in a comparison.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal supernatural dream event or identify the dreamer as a particular person.

title: Closed eyes
summary: The passage addresses evildoers, describing them as crying out, staggering as if drunken, and having closed their eyes and rejected the prophets. Their rulers and seers are covered because of their iniquity.

explicit_facts.text: Evildoers will cry out and stagger, though not from wine or strong drink.
The Lord has poured out a spirit of deep sleep; the people have closed their eyes and rejected the prophets, and their rulers and seers are covered because of iniquity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Closed eyes can symbolize rejection and spiritual sleep.
unspecified_visual_details: No particular evildoers, rulers, or seers are identified or described.

narration.text: ye have closed your eyes
ye have rejected the prophets

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The deep sleep and covered rulers/seers are stated figuratively; avoid visualizing them as literal supernatural effects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named people, a specific public gathering, or literal intoxication.

title: The book brought forth
summary: The Lord God will bring forth the words of a book—the words of those who have slumbered. The book will be sealed and contain a revelation spanning the beginning to the end of the world; its sealed contents will be withheld from the people in their wickedness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will bring the words of a book to the people; they are the words of those who have slumbered.
The book will be sealed and contain a revelation from the beginning of the world to its ending.
The sealed things will not be delivered in the day of the people’s wickedness, and the book will be kept from them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A book with some portion sealed may represent the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The book’s material, appearance, location, and possessor are not specified here.

narration.text: the Lord God shall bring forth unto you the words of a book
the book shall be sealed

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This passage foretells events; the book’s bringing forth is not presented as a current visual event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the book’s title, physical design, or an identifiable person holding it.

title: The book delivered
summary: The book will be delivered to a man, who will deliver its words to another, but not the sealed words. The sealed revelation will remain in the book until the Lord’s due time.

explicit_facts.text: A man will receive the book and deliver its words to another.
He will not deliver the sealed words; the sealed revelation will remain in the book until the Lord’s due time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy may be represented by a book passed between two unidentified figures.
unspecified_visual_details: The men’s identities, appearance, location, and the book’s appearance are not specified.

narration.text: the book shall be delivered unto a man
he shall deliver these words unto another

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The delivery is prophetic, not an event expressly narrated as happening in the present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the men names or biographies, or show them as historically identified individuals.

title: Words on the housetops
summary: A day will come when the sealed words are read upon the housetops by the power of Christ, and all things will be revealed to the children of men through the end of the earth.

explicit_facts.text: The sealed words will be read upon the housetops by the power of Christ; all things will be revealed to the children of men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A housetop can serve as the setting for an illustration of the prophesied reading.
unspecified_visual_details: The reader, listeners, specific housetop, and visible manifestation of Christ are not described.

narration.text: the words of the book which were sealed shall be read upon the house tops

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a future prophecy, not a witnessed present-day scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ visibly or invent the reader or listeners.

title: Witnesses see the book
summary: When the book is delivered to the man, it will be hidden from the world’s eyes. Three witnesses besides him, and a few others according to God’s will, will see it and testify.

explicit_facts.text: When the book is delivered to the man, it will be hidden from the world except for three witnesses who will see it by God’s power and testify of its truth and contents.
A few others according to God’s will will view it to bear testimony of God’s word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The prophecy may be represented by a man and three witnesses viewing a book, while others remain outside the view.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities, appearance, location, and number of the additional few are unspecified.

narration.text: three witnesses shall behold it
they shall testify to the truth of the book

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The witnesses seeing the book is a future event in this passage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the witnesses or depict the book’s supernatural concealment as a visible effect.

title: Witnesses establish the word
summary: The Lord God will bring forth the words of the book and establish his word through as many witnesses as he sees fit; woe is pronounced on one who rejects God’s word.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will bring forth the book’s words and establish his word through as many witnesses as seemeth him good.
Woe is pronounced upon the one who rejects the word of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group of unnamed witnesses could be shown as a symbolic representation of the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The witnesses’ number, identities, appearance, and setting are not specified.

narration.text: in the mouth of as many witnesses as seemeth him good will he establish his word

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a prophecy and warning, not a separately narrated gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent named witnesses or depict a divine figure.

title: The learned are asked to read
summary: The Lord God will tell the man to take the unsealed words to another, who will show them to the learned and ask them to read. The learned will request the book for the glory of the world and gain, not God’s glory.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will direct the man to deliver the unsealed words to another, who will show them to the learned and ask them to read.
The learned will ask for the book because of worldly glory and gain, not the glory of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An unidentified man may present written words to an unidentified learned person.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, place, written words, and book are not visually described.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The learned

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The speech is reported as a future exchange; use off-screen speech over an unspecified setting rather than implying the exchange is currently occurring.

title: The book is sealed

The learned person will say he cannot read it.

unspecified_visual_details: The participants’ identities, appearances, and location are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: I cannot bring the book, for it is sealed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The man

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a reported future exchange, not a present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give either speaker a name or a specific physical appearance.

title: The unlearned man
summary: The Lord God will again deliver the book and its words to a man who is not learned. The man will say he is not learned. The Lord God will tell him to read the words given to him and not to touch the sealed things.
characters: The man that is not learned
The Lord God (speaker; no appearance described)

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God will again deliver the book and its words to a man who is not learned; the man will say he is not learned.
The Lord God will say the learned will not read the words because they have rejected them, and will tell the man to read the words given to him.
The Lord God will tell him not to touch the sealed things and will bring them forth in his own due time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord God's speech can be represented without showing a divine form.
unspecified_visual_details: The man's identity and appearance are not specified.
The location and means of delivering the book are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The man that is not learned

spoken_dialogue.text: The learned shall not read them, for they have rejected them, and I am able to do mine own work;

spoken_dialogue.text: Touch not the things which are sealed, for I will bring them forth in mine own due time;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord God

title: Read, witness, and preserve
summary: The Lord instructs the man to read the commanded words, obtain the promised witnesses, then seal the book again and hide it until the Lord sees fit to reveal all things. The Lord declares himself God of miracles and says he works among people according to their faith.

explicit_facts.text: After reading the commanded words and obtaining the promised witnesses, the man is to seal the book again and hide it, preserving unread words until God chooses to reveal all things.
God declares himself a God of miracles, the same yesterday, today, and forever, and says he works among people according to their faith.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A book being sealed and hidden may represent the instruction, without specifying a method or place.
unspecified_visual_details: The man, witnesses, book design, and hiding place are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: seal up the book again, and hide it up unto me
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord God

narration.text: I am God; and I am a God of miracles

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The instructions and declaration are reported speech; do not invent a visible miracle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a specific miracle or identify the man or witnesses.

title: A marvelous work
summary: The Lord will speak to the one who reads the delivered words, describing a people who honor him with their lips while their hearts are far from him. He will do a marvelous work, and the wisdom and understanding of the wise and prudent will perish or be hidden.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord will speak to the one who reads the delivered words.
The people draw near with their mouths and lips but have removed their hearts far from the Lord; their fear of him is taught by human precepts.
The Lord will do a marvelous work and a wonder, and the wisdom of the wise and learned will perish and the understanding of the prudent be hidden.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Lord’s teaching may be presented as off-screen speech over a general setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The people and the one who reads are not identified or described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Forasmuch as this people draw near unto me with their mouth, and with their lips do honor me, but have removed their hearts far from me, and their fear towards me is taught by the precepts of men—
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

narration.text: I will proceed to do a marvelous work among this people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The scene reports the Lord’s teaching and prophecy; do not literalize the figurative hiding or perishing of understanding.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a miraculous event or assign identities to the people.

title: Counsel in darkness
summary: The Lord condemns those who hide counsel from him and ask who sees or knows them. He declares that he knows their works and challenges the idea that a thing made can deny or misunderstand its maker.

explicit_facts.text: Some seek to hide counsel from the Lord and do their works in darkness, asking who sees or knows them.
They compare turning things upside down to a potter’s clay; the Lord says he knows all their works and asks whether a made thing can deny or misunderstand its maker.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Darkness and pottery imagery may illustrate the teaching symbolically.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, objects, and setting are not specifically identified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Who seeth us, and who knoweth us?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Those who hide counsel

spoken_dialogue.text: For shall the work say of him that made it, he made me not?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord of Hosts

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The potter and made-work language is figurative teaching, not a narrated supernatural scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the metaphorical objects as speaking literal dialogue.

title: A fruitful field

explicit_facts.text: The Lord of Hosts says Lebanon will be turned into a fruitful field and the fruitful field esteemed as a forest.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A landscape contrasting cultivated field and forest may represent the prophecy.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a future prophetic description.

title: The deaf hear, the blind see
summary: In that day, the deaf will hear the words of the book and the blind will see out of obscurity and darkness. The meek will increase and rejoice in the Lord, and the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

explicit_facts.text: In that day the deaf will hear the book’s words and the blind will see out of obscurity and darkness.
The meek will increase and have joy in the Lord; the poor among men will rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The promised hearing and seeing may be shown as a future outcome, without suggesting a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, their identities, and setting are not specified.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse is prophetic and does not identify particular deaf, blind, meek, or poor individuals.

title: The unjust are cut off
summary: The terrible one, scorner, and those watching for iniquity will be brought to naught or cut off. The passage also names those who accuse a man for a word, snare one who reproves at the gate, and turn aside the just for nothing.

explicit_facts.text: The terrible one will be brought to naught, the scorner consumed, and those who watch for iniquity cut off.
The passage describes people who make a man an offender for a word, lay a snare for one who reproves in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of naught.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The injustice may be conveyed through restrained symbolic imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The people and any specific incidents are not identified or described.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses summarize prophetic judgment and wrongdoing, not a specific present-time confrontation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a named accuser, victim, or actual injury.

title: Concerning the house of Jacob
summary: Nephi attributes to the Lord a prophecy concerning the house of Jacob: Jacob will not be ashamed or pale; his children will sanctify the Lord’s name and the Holy One of Jacob and fear the God of Israel; those who erred or murmured will gain understanding and learn doctrine.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi attributes the words concerning the house of Jacob to the Lord, who redeemed Abraham.
Jacob shall not be ashamed, nor shall his face grow pale.
When Jacob sees his children in his midst, they shall sanctify the Lord’s name and the Holy One of Jacob and fear the God of Israel.
Those who erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and those who murmured shall learn doctrine.

unspecified_visual_details: No location, physical appearances, or visible occasion for this prophecy is specified.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the prophecy as a present-time event or invent an appearance for the Lord.
